names_for.catalogue_side: 'data licensing' / 'datasets' (filings: 'data offering', 'data deals'); contributors see a 'Data Catalog'
names_for.custom_side: 'custom datasets' within its 'AI services' for model builders; 'tailored services' to curate datasets; Shutterstock Studios for custom content production

operator_role.note: Contributors grant Shutterstock a sublicensable non-exclusive licence; Shutterstock itself licenses datasets to buyers (and is the 'Provider' on its AWS listing).

economics_model.note: Shutterstock keeps the revenue from data deals and pays about 20% on average into a pooled Contributor Fund.

who_pays_fee.note: No buyer-side fee is published; Shutterstock's share comes out of the deal value, since contributors get a share (about 20% on average) of the contract value.

supply_models.note: Contributor uploads, both creative-marketplace content and data-only 'Data Catalog' content. No evidence found of own speculative collections or third-party dataset providers being listed; custom datasets from production hubs are made to order.

custody_model.note: Large metadata sets are delivered to customers (revenue is recognised on delivery); the AWS sample is exported to the buyer's S3.

transaction_mode.note: Only the 1,000-image sample is self-serve (free on AWS). Full-library data goes through sales.

public_prices.note: No dataset price was found in filings, press or the AWS listing (only the free sample, $0). shutterstock.com returned 403, so its data-licensing page could not be checked.

licence_model.note: A research licence and a commercial licence are offered, but deals are individual contracts, some multi-year and some cancellable. Use is limited to ML/CV training.

exclusivity_offered.note: Not published. Contributor content is non-exclusive, which suggests but does not prove that no exclusivity is sold.

public_listing.note: shutterstock.com returned 403. The only public dataset listing seen is the free AWS Data Exchange sample.

sample_mechanics.note: Free 1,000-image sample with metadata on AWS Data Exchange.

versioning.note: The AWS sample gives access to all historical and future revisions, but nothing is published about versioning of negotiated data deliveries.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Releases are collected and reviewed but not given to customers; buyers get a has_model_release flag and a model_release_id.

contributor_pay_model.note: A pooled Contributor Fund (about 20% of data-licence revenue on average), paid pro rata to the volume of each contributor's content in the datasets sold, every six months.

erasure_after_sale.note: Opt-out affects only future datasets, and licences for removed content stay in force in perpetuity. The AWS standard DSA on the free sample does require deletion when the licence ends [c100].

quality_evidence.note: Every submission is reviewed by Shutterstock. Data Catalog content can be content rejected for creative quality, but it still passes legal and IP review.

Q1.answer: AI and ML model builders, from large tech and media companies to start-ups (OpenAI, Meta, NVIDIA, Runway and others by the vendor's account), license images, video, music and 3D with metadata under large multi-year contracts. Data revenue is lumpy and fell 26% in H1 2026.

Q2.answer: Shutterstock sells direct but lists a free 1,000-image sample on AWS Data Exchange as a funnel to its sales team. The AWS listing brings discovery and S3 delivery, and the sale itself stays off-platform.

Q3.answer: Inventory is contributor uploads licensed non-exclusively to Shutterstock, including data-only content rejected from the creative library. Contributors can opt out by media type (from 2023/2024) and are paid from a pooled fund.

Q4.answer: Datasets launched in July 2021, but the opt-out came only in January 2023 and applies only to future datasets. The terms can be changed at any time, and the press questioned contributor consent. No evidence was found on commissioned-work carve-outs.

Q5.answer: Shutterstock is licensor of record under a sublicensable contributor licence. Contributors warrant releases and indemnify Shutterstock. On AWS, Shutterstock as Provider indemnifies subscribers. The buyer-side data deal terms are not published.

Q6.answer: Copied to the buyer: large metadata sets are delivered, with revenue recognised on delivery, and the AWS sample is exported to S3.

Q7.answer: Capturers: per-media opt-out toggles for future datasets. Depicted people: a release is required for every identifiable person and reviewed, but it is not shared with buyers, who get only a flag and ID. Property: releases are checked in review.

Q8.answer: Use is limited to ML/CV training, with research or commercial licences. On the AWS sample, the standard DSA bars redistribution and requires deletion on termination. No audit, fingerprinting or leakage terms were found.

Q9.answer: Contact sales ('start the conversation', or email the sales team). Shutterstock owns the licence and pays contributors about 20% of revenue on average. Contracts are multi-year, some with cancellation rights.

Q10.answer: A dataset is a set of assets plus metadata, tracked in an internal database of every asset used in every dataset. Deliveries are timed in contracts. Only the AWS sample documents revisions; nothing is published on withdrawals.

Q11.answer: A free 1,000-image sample with a metadata schema (release flags, demographics). Buyers otherwise rely on Shutterstock's review process and its 'ethically sourced', provenance claims.

Q12.answer: Off-the-shelf 'data licensing'/'datasets' sit alongside 'custom datasets' made through its 'AI services', using production hubs and the contributor network. Submissions qualify for Creative Licensing, Data Licensing or both.

sections.positioning: Shutterstock is a public stock-media company whose 'data offering' licenses metadata tied to its images, footage, music and 3D models for AI training [c017][c054]. It markets this data to investors as 'ethically sourced' [c020]. The data offering is reported inside Data, Distribution, and Services, alongside Giphy and Studios [c021].
sections.supply: All inventory comes from contributor uploads licensed non-exclusively [c078][c080]. Accepted content is also made available to data partners [c042]. From June 2023 submissions are routed to creative, data or both [c071][c070], and content rejected on quality can go to a data-only Data Catalog [c066][c033]. From 2024 this includes video [c073]. Opt-out toggles exist since 2023 and are split by media type since 2024 [c031][c032]. AI-generated uploads are barred [c039].
sections.object_model: Datasets combine assets with metadata: images, video, 3D and music [c036]. The metadata includes release flags, a model_release_id and model age, gender and ethnicity [c094][c095], plus titles and keywords [c105]. An internal database records every asset used in every dataset, for paying contributors [c030].
sections.listing: No public dataset catalogue was reachable (shutterstock.com returned 403). The one public listing found is a free 1,000-image sample on AWS Data Exchange [c090].
sections.trust: A release is required for every identifiable person [c076], and since 2023 releases must include a date of birth [c074]. Releases are not shared with customers [c059][c061]. Shutterstock markets its data as having clear provenance [c110]. The press has questioned contributor consent [c128].
sections.transaction: Deals go through sales: buyers email the team or 'start the conversation' [c092][c111]. Contracts can run for years [c050][c129], and some carry cancellation rights [c051][c052].
sections.pricing: No dataset prices were found. The only priced item is the free sample [c091]. The February 2024 deck implies about $10 million a year per anchor data customer [c119].
sections.licence: Buyers may use datasets only to train ML and computer-vision models [c026]. There is a research licence and a commercial licence [c106]. The AWS sample uses AWS's standard DSA [c098][c099][c102].
sections.custody: Data is delivered to the buyer, and revenue follows delivery timing [c016][c053]. The AWS sample is exported to S3 [c103].
sections.vetting: Each submission is reviewed by technology and human reviewers [c046], including for releases and third-party IP [c045][c072]. Shutterstock may refuse any content [c087].
sections.contributor_pay: Data revenue is pooled in a Contributor Fund [c028], which pays about 20% of data-licence revenue on average [c027]. Each share is pro rata to the volume of the contributor's content in the datasets sold [c029], drawn from the whole contract value [c124]. Payouts come every six months [c068] in a separate 'Contributor Fund' column [c038]. Contributors see which files were accepted in the Data Catalog [c034], but not the dataset buyers [c125]. Creative licences pay per-download tiered royalties [c043].
sections.post_sale: Opt-out affects future datasets only [c122], and licences for removed content survive in perpetuity [c081]. The AWS DSA requires deletion when the licence ends [c100].
sections.catalogue_custom: Alongside the catalogue, Shutterstock offers tailored dataset curation [c093] and AI services launched in October 2025 [c112]. These include custom datasets from 10 production hubs and more than 2 million creators [c113], plus annotation [c114]. The plan to use contributors for 'bespoke data training sets' dates to 2024 [c118].
sections.changes: The Getty merger ended on 7 July 2026 [c002]. A $173.7 million goodwill impairment followed [c006], then a CEO exit [c004] and a dividend suspension [c005]. The company had already cut more than $70 million of run-rate costs and is targeting $60 million more [c007][c008]. New directors were appointed on 8 September 2026 [c001].
sections.demand: Data revenue grew 15% in 2024 [c049]. The segment containing it grew 16% in 2025 on metadata sales [c047][c048]. In 2026 data revenue fell 11% in Q2 and 26% in H1 [c014][c015]. The buyers named are OpenAI and other AI labs [c127][c108][c115].
sections.regulation: The 10-K flags the EU Data Act and AI Act as possible limits on data use [c058].

buyer_journey.step: A prospective buyer reads a Shutterstock announcement and is directed to shutterstock.com/data-licensing to 'start the conversation'. That page returned 403 to our fetcher, so what it shows is unknown.
Alternatively, the buyer finds Shutterstock's free 1,000-image sample on AWS Data Exchange. It is drawn from a library of more than 550 million images.
The buyer subscribes to the sample at no charge and accepts the vendor EULA, which is AWS's standard Data Subscription Agreement.

The buyer exports the sample to S3 and inspects the images and CSV metadata, including has_model_release flags and model age, gender and ethnicity fields. The release documents themselves are not included.
For full-library data, the buyer emails Shutterstock's sales team, which offers tailored curation or custom collection.
The buyer negotiates a contract. It may start with a research licence and move to a commercial one; deals can be multi-year and some carry cancellation rights.
Shutterstock delivers the content and metadata sets on a contracted schedule, and use is restricted to ML and computer-vision training.

conflicts.resolution: Filings describe the data offering as licensing 'metadata' tied to assets, while the contributor help centre says datasets include content and metadata. They are probably the same product described narrowly and broadly; the buyer contract would settle it but was not reachable.

Library size is cited as 370M+ (AWS blog, 2021), 550M+ (AWS listing, undated) and 771M images (investor deck, February 2024). These are different dates rather than a contradiction; the newest filing-dated figure is 771M.
